stem: Use of polished rice in human diet causes the following disease
expl: White rice is milled rice that had its husk, bran, and germ removed. After milling, the rice is polished, resulting in a seed with a bright, white, shiny appearance. The milling and polishing processes of polished rice both remove nutrients. A diet based on polished rice leaves many people vulnerable to the neurological disease beriberi, due to a deficiency of thiamine (Vitamin B). Adopted over brown rice in the second half of the 19th century because it was favoured by traders, white rice has led to a beriberi epidemic in Asia (Including British India).

stem: The ‘blue baby’ pollution disease is due to the excessive presence of which of the following in drinking water ?
expl: Blue baby syndrome is an illness that begins when a large amount of nitrates in water (or food) are ingested by an infant and converted to nitrite by the digestive system. The nitrite then reacts with oxyhaemoglobin to form methemoglobin, which cannot carry oxygen. If a large amount of methemoglobin is formed in the blood, body tissues may be deprived of oxygen, causing the infant to develop a blue coloration of their mucous membranes and possibly digestive and respiratory problems. This condition is also known as methemoglobinemia.

stem: ‘Metastasis’ is the process by which :

options.label: a
options.text: Cells divide rapidly under the influence of drugs

options.label: b
options.text: Cancer cells spread through the blood or lymphatic system to other sites or organs

options.label: c
options.text: The chromosomes in cells nuclei are attached to the spindle before moving to the anaphase poles

options.label: d
options.text: Cancer cells are successfully inhibited to divide any further

expl: The process by which cancer cells spread to other parts of the body is called metastasis. Cancer cells metastasis usually involves the following steps : Local invasion – Cancer cells invade nearby normal tissue. Intravasation – Cancer cells invade and move through the walls of nearby lymph vessels or blood vessels. Circulation – Cancer cells move through the lymphatic system and the bloodstream to other parts of the body. Arrest and extravasation – Cancer cells arrest or stop moving in small blood vessels called capillaries at a distant location. Then invade the walls of the capillaries and migrate into surrounding tissue (extravasation). Proliferation – Cancer cells multiply at the distant location to form small tumours known as micrometastases. Angiogenesis – Micrometastases stimulate the growth of new blood vessels to obtain a blood supply. A blood supply is needed to obtain the oxygen and nutrients necessary for continued tumor (neoplasm) growth. Because cancers of the lymphatic system or the blood system are already present in lymph vessels lymph nodes or blood vessels, not all of these steps are needed for their metastasis.

expl: Our liver stores glycogen to fulfil body’s requirement of glucose for energy in between meals. This storage is recouped after every meal. If the meal is delayed further, the body starts consuming its fat reserve and proteins. This condition is starvation. Prolonged starvation causes Marasmus due to a generalized wasting of the body because of both energy and protein deficiency. Due to this, the body of children becomes lean and weak, eyes depressed and skin wrinkled.

stem: Which one of the following pairs matches one another?
expl: Cataract – Eye Jaundice – Liver Typhoid – Intestine Pneumonia – Lungs

expl: The correctly matched pairs are : Pneumonia – Lungs Cataract – Eye Jaundice – Liver Diabetes – Metabolism

stem: Astigmatism is a disease of the :
expl: Astigmatism is a common and usually minor eye condition that causes blurred or distorted vision. It occurs when the cornea or lens is not in a perfectly curved shape. Many people who wear glasses have some degree of astigmatism. It belongs to a group of related eye conditions known as refractive errors. Other common refractive errors include- short-sightedness (myopia) and long-sightedness (hypermetropia).

stem: Myopia is the disorder of which organ?
expl: Near-sightedness, also known as short-sightedness and myopia is a condition of the eye where the light focuses in front of, instead of on the retina. This causes the distant objects to be blurry, while the close objects appear normal. Other symptoms may include a headache and eye strain.

stem: Myopia or short sightedness is corrected by :
expl: Myopia or near-sightedness is corrected by using a concave lens. It is a refractive error, which means that the eye does not bend or refract light properly to a single focus to see images clearly. In myopia, close or nearby objects look clear but distant objects appear blurred. A myopic eye forms the image of a far-off object in front of the retina because of the increase in converging power of the eye lens.

stem: A person with vision defect ‘Myopia’ can see –

options.label: c
options.text: Nearby as well as distant objects clearly

options.label: d
options.text: Neither nearby nor distant objects clearly

expl: Near-sightedness or myopia as it is medically termed, is a vision condition in which close objects are seen clearly, but objects faraway appear blurred. It can be corrected by wearing concave or divergent lenses.

stem: The person is suffering from far-sightedness face difficulties in–

options.label: c
options.text: To see both close and distant object clearly

expl: Hypermetropia or far-sightedness or long-sightedness is a vision defect in which the image of nearer objects is blurred due to its being formed beyond retina due to eyeball being short or lens being flattened. It is corrected by wearing (spectacles with) convex or convergent lenses.

stem: In which part of eye ‘blind spot’ and ‘yellow spot’ are found?
expl: Blind spot and yellow spot both are found in the retina. The area of the retina where optic nerve and blood vessels enter and leave the eyeball is called blind spot (optic disc) as it does not contain visual cells. An area lateral to and above the blind spot is the spot of image formation. It is called yellow area or macula lutea. Its central 1.5 mm area is depressed and devoid of blood vessels as well as nerve fibres. It is called yellow spot or fovea centralis. It lies on the optical axis, has a maximum density of cone cells and forms the sharpest vision.

stem: The retina is outgrowth of the –
expl: The retina develops as an outgrowth from the brain (diencephalon). The proximal part of the diverticulum remains narrow and is called the optic stalk. It later becomes the optic nerve. The distal part of the diverticulum forms rounded hollow structure called optic vesicle. This vesicle is invaginated by the developing lens so that it gets converted into a two layered optic cup.

stem: If the lens in eye becomes opaque, the disease is called
expl: In older persons the eye lenses become opaque reducing visibility. This is called cataract. Cataract can be nuclear (central portion opacity) or cortical (peripheral opacity). Cataract is corrected by (i) removing of the opaque lens and wearing special spectacles, (ii) replacing the opaque lens with artificial intracular lens, and (iii) laser treatment of opacity.

stem: Which part of human eye is affected by cataract?
expl: In older persons the eye lenses become opaque reducing visibility. This is called cataract. Cataract can be nuclear (central portion opacity) or cortical (peripheral opacity). Cataract is corrected by (i) removing of the opaque lens and wearing special spectacles, (ii) replacing the opaque lens with artificial intracular lens, and (iii) laser treatment of opacity.

stem: In cataract the natural lens becomes cloudy because of change in which of the following?
expl: Around age of 40 years and above, the proteins in the natural lens of human eye start to break down and clump together. This clump makes a cloudy area on human lens – known as a cataract. Over time, the cataract gets worse and makes more of natural lens cloudy. For people who have cataracts, seeing through cloudy lenses is like looking through a frosty or fogged-up window. Clouded vision caused by cataracts can make it more difficult to read, drive a car at night or see the expression on a friend's face.

stem:
Match List-I (Drugs/Chemicals) with List-II (Their uses) and select the correct answer using the codes given below :
List-I List-II
A. Atropine 1. Local anaesthesia
B. Ether 2. Heart trouble
C. Nitroglycerine 3. Dilation of pupil
D. Pyrethrin 4. Mosquito control
Code : A B C D
expl: Topical atropine is used as a cycloplegic, to temporarily paralyze the accommodation reflex and as a mydriatic to dilate the pupils. Ether is an organic compound in the ether class with the formula R-O-R′. It is commonly used as a local anaesthetic. For over 140 years, nitroglycerine has been used medically as a potent vasodilator to treat heart conditions, such as angina pectoris and chronic heart failure. The pyrethrins are a class of organic compounds normally derived from Chrysanthemum cinerarii folium that have potent insecticidal activity by targeting the nervous systems of insects.

stem: The pupils of human eye are dilated with a very dilute solution of an alkaloid which is :
expl: Atropine occurs naturally and is extracted from belladonna alkaloids contained in plants. Ophthalmic atropine is used during eye examinations to dilate the pupil.

stem: The Ishihara test is related with :
expl: The Ishihara Test is the most well known colour blindness test all around the world. It is a colour vision test for detection of red-green colour deficiencies. It was named after its designer, Shinobu Ishihara, a professor at the University of Tokyo, who first published his tests in 1917. Full IshiharaTest consists of 38 so called pseudoisochromatic plates, each of them showing either a number or some lines. According to what you can see and what not, the test gives feedback of the degree of your red-green colour vision deficiency. There are also Ishihara tests consisting of 10, 14 or 24 test plates.

stem: Deficiency of Iron causes –
expl: Anaemia is a condition in which the body does not have enough healthy red blood cells. Our body requires about 12 milligram of iron per day. Red blood cells provide oxygen to body tissues. There are many types of anaemia. Iron deficiency anaemia occurs when your body does not have enough iron. Iron helps to make red blood cells. Iron is a key part of red blood cells. It is the main component of haemoglobin and cytochrome enzyme.

stem: The disease caused due to deficiency of iron is known as–
expl: Anaemia is a condition in which the body does not have enough healthy red blood cells. Our body requires about 12 milligram of iron per day. Red blood cells provide oxygen to body tissues. It is the main component of haemoglobin and cytochrome enzyme.

stem: Which of the following disease is caused by the excessive use of alcoholic beverage ?
expl: Liver cirrhosis is a serious condition where normal liver tissues are replaced by scar tissues (fibrosis). It is caused by the excessive use of alcoholic beverage. It tends to progress slowly and often does not cause symptoms in its early stage. However as the function of the liver gradually becomes worse, serious problems can develop.

stem: Oral submucous fibrosis is a disease caused by –
expl: Oral submucous fibrosis is a chronic debilitating disease of the oral cavity characterized by inflammation and progressive fibrosis of the submucosal tissues. Oral submucous fibrosis is a premalignant condition caused mainly due to chewing of betel quid or areca nuts. Gutka is a manufactured version of betel quid.

stem: Jaundice affects the –
expl: Jaundice, a yellowish pigmentation of the skin, the conjunctival membranes over the sclera and other mucous membranes caused by high blood bilirubin levels. This hyperbilirubinemia subsequently causes increased levels of bilirubin in the extracellular fluid. Jaundice affects the liver. Jaundice is often seen in liver diseases such as hepatitis or liver cancer. It may also indicate leptospirosis or obstruction of the biliary tract, for example by gallstones or pancreatic cancer.

stem: Which disease is not so contagious ?
expl: Jaundice is not an infectious disease, while other three are. During jaundice, skin and eyes become yellowish, urine becomes yellowish-greenish and wastes become brownish.

stem: Rickets disease in poultry bird is caused due to the deficiency of which vitamin?
expl: Rickets is defective mineralization or calcification of bones in immature mammals particularly in humans and chickens due to deficiency or impaired metabolism of vitamin D, phosphorus or calcium. It potentially leads to fractures and deformity.

stem: The factor of madcow disease is–
expl: Madcow is a dangerous disease related to the brain of cattle. Distorted protein ‘prion’ in their brain is the factor of it.

stem: Liver fluke in bile duct remains in–
expl: Liver fluke is a common endoparasite in the larger bile ducts and passage of the liver of sheep and hence commonly called ‘sheep liver fluke’. It can also develop in pig, goats etc. Mammals are its primary host and snail is its secondary or intermediate host.

stem: Bright’s disease affects human body in the part –
expl: Bright’s disease is a kidney disorder. In Bright’s disease, the blood vessels in the kidneys are inflamed and albumin is excreted in the urine. It is also known as nephritis and can be acute or chronic.

stem: Pneumoconiosis affects the workers who work mainly in :
expl: Pneumoconiosis is an occupational and restrictive lung disease caused by the inhalation of dust, often in mines. This affect the lungs of miners and they feel difficulty in breathing.

stem: The blood glucose level is commonly expressed as :
expl: The blood glucose level is commonly expressed as milligram per decilitre or mmol/L. When operating normally the body restores blood sugar level to a range of about 4.4 to 6.1 mmol/L (82 to 110 milligram per decilitre). Shortly after meal, the blood glucose level may rise temporarily up to about 7.8 mmol/L (140 milligram per decilitre).

stem: Ramu injects an injection in an excess amount. In result, he suffers from spasm, apoplexy and faintness and dies later. The reason is –

options.label: d
options.text: Lack of calcium ion in blood

expl: Spasm, apoplexy and faintness are the result of unusual glucose concentration in blood. Insulin hormone regulates sugar in the blood.

stem: Which one of the following diseases can not be controlled by vaccination?
expl: Polio, whooping cough and smallpox can control by vaccination but there is no vaccination available for diabetes. Diabetes is a disease related to pancreas which is caused due to insufficient amount of insulin in the blood.

stem: Diabetes is the most common disorder associated with:
expl: Diabetes is a chronic disease that occurs either when the pancreas does not produce enough insulin or when the body cannot effectively use the insulin it produces. Insulin is a hormone that regulates blood glucose. Insulin is produced in the pancreas and is synthesized in the pancreas within the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans. Hyperglycaemia, also called raised blood glucose or raised blood sugar, is a common effect of uncontrolled diabetes and over time leads to serious damage to many of the body's systems, especially the nerves and blood vessels. Diabetes may cause blindness, kidney failure, heart attacks, stroke and lower limb amputation etc.

stem: Lack of which substance causes diabetes in a person?
expl: Insulin is a hormone made in the pancreas, that allows our body to use sugar (glucose) from carbohydrates in the food that we eat for energy or to store glucose for future use. Insulin helps to keep blood sugar level from getting too high (hyperglycemia) or too low (hypoglycemia). Lack of Insulin in the body causes diabetes in a person. Diabetes patients have excess urination problem called polyuria.

stem:
Which of the following are associated with diabetes mellitus, a common disease in adults ?
1. Higher sugar level in blood
2. Lower sugar level in blood
3. Lower insulin level in blood
4. Higher insulin level in blood
Select the correct answer by using the codes given below:
expl: When a low level of insulin is secreted from β-cells of pancreatic islets of Langerhans, sugar level enhances in the blood. As the result of it, the probability of diabetes gets increased.

stem: Measurement of glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) in the blood is useful for the management of :
expl: Measurement of glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) in the blood is used for the management of diabetes mellitus. The glycosylated haemoglobin test shows what a person's average blood glucose level was for the 8 to 12 weeks before the test.

stem:
Assertion (A) : T he person with diabetes insipidus feels thirsty.
Reason (R) : A person with diabetes insipidus suffers from excess secretion of vasopressin.

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: Diabetes insipidus is a rare condition where one produces a large amount of urine and often feels thirsty. It is caused by problems with a hormone called antidiuretic hormone (ADH), also known as vasopressin. ADH plays a key role in regulating the amount of urine in the body. In diabetes insipidus, the lack of production of ADH causes too much water to be passed from the body.

stem:
Assertion (A) : Drinking of whiskey increases the frequency of urination.
Reason (R) : Alcohol intake speeds up the secretion of vasopressin in the body.
Code :

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: Drinking of whiskey increases the frequency of urination because it behaves like a diuretic substance that increases urine production in the body. Alcohol also suppresses secretion of pituitary gland hormone vasopressin (ADH) which is responsible for inhibiting the diuretic effect. This makes our kidneys unable to reabsorb as much liquid as usual. This result in a substantial increase in urine output.

stem: Which one of the following seeds can benefit a patient of diabetes mellitus by normalizing his blood sugar level?
expl: Fenugreek seeds help in slow absorption of sugar in the stomach and stimulate insulin. Both of these effects lower blood sugar in people with diabetes. These seeds are helpful in maintenance of cholesterol level and triglyceraldehyde in the human body. It is beneficiary to cure breast cancer and colon cancer also because its major systematics deals with digestion.

stem: Curry leaf tree, native of India has the potential of a multi-billion dollar production for the pharmaceutical companies as revealed by British researchers, a cure for which disease is claimed for the curry leaf ?
expl: Curry leaf tree, a native of India has the potential of multi-billion dollar production for the pharmaceutical companies as revealed by British researchers. It is beneficial in the medication of diabetes. Diabetes is caused due to lackness of insulin hormone.

stem: The hormone insulin which is used in treating diabetes was discovered by –
expl: Two Canadian Scientist, Banting & Best prepared an active infusion of hormone insulin with help of Macleod in 1923. Banting & Macleod got Nobel Prize (1923) for this scientific research. Insulin hormone is related to regulation of glucose in the blood.

stem: A commonest side effect of Cu-T :
expl: Copper-T is an effective contraceptive and is one of the most immensely used methods of birth control worldwide. Although this method is very effective and widely used, it comes with some side effects also. Many women experience more bleeding during the menstrual cycle after the insertion of copper-T.

stem: Emphysema is a disease caused by environmental pollution in which the affected organ of the body is
expl: Emphysema is one of the several diseases known collectively as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) by which lungs of human gets affected.

stem: Which statement about aspirin is not true?

options.label: a
options.text: It is a neurologically active drug.

options.label: c
options.text: It is effective in relieving pain.

options.label: d
options.text: It has anti blood clotting action.

expl: Aspirin, also known as acetylsalicylic acid is a neurologically active drug which is used to treat pain, fever and inflammation. Aspirin is also used long-term at low doses, to help prevent heart attacks, strokes and blood clot formation in people. Aspirin belongs to non-narcotic analgesics.

stem: CPR stands for :
expl: CPR, or cardiopulmonary resuscitation, is an emergency life-saving procedure performed when someone's breathing or heartbeat has stopped, consisting of chest compressions often combined with artificial ventilation, or mouth-to-mouth in an effort to manually preserve and rescue breaths to maintain blood flow and oxygenation until medical help arrives. CPR is used on people in cardiac arrest to oxygenate the blood and maintain a cardiac output to keep vital organs alive. Immediate CPR can double or triple chances of survival after cardiac arrest.

stem: In coronary artery bypass surgery, the blood vessel to be used as graft has to be –

options.label: c
options.text: Artery from mammary region of chest

expl: In Coronary Artery Disease (CAD), the arteries that supply blood and oxygen to the heart muscle grow hardened and narrowed. Coronary artery bypass surgery creates a new path for blood to flow to the heart. The surgeon takes a healthy piece of vein from the leg or artery from the chest or wrist. Then the surgeon attaches it to the coronary artery, just above and below the narrowed area or blockage. This allows blood to bypass (get around) the blockage.

stem: In which of the following departments of a hospital will ‘Cath lab’ be found ?
expl: A catheterization laboratory or cath lab is a clinic with diagnostic imaging equipment used to visualize the arteries of the heart and the chambers of the heart and treat any stenosis or abnormality found. The cardiology cath lab area is, where all invasive cardiology investigations and treatments are undertaken.

stem: The nutritional deficiency condition that needs to be given top priority for remedial action in India today is :
expl: Xerophthalmia, caused by severe vitamin A deficiency, is described by, pathological dryness of conjunctiva and cornea. Cells of cornea get dried, keratinized and vision power affected. That’s why remedial action for Xeropthalmia should be prioritized.

stem: Lathyrism is caused by excessive consumption of :
expl: Excessive consumption of khesari dal (Lathyrus sativus) can lead to lathyrism, a neurological disorder characterized by muscle weakness, spasms, and paralysis, particularly of the lower limbs.
